title: 'Tis So Sweet to Trust in Jesus
author: Louisa M. R. Stead

slides.text:
'Tis so sweet to trust in Jesus,
And to take Him at His word;
Just to rest upon His promise,
And to know, Thus says the Lord!
slides.label: Verse 1

slides.text:
Jesus, Jesus, how I trust Him!
How I've proved Him o'er and o'er;
Jesus, Jesus, precious Jesus!
O for grace to trust Him more!
slides.label: Chorus

slides.text:
O how sweet to trust in Jesus,
Just to trust His cleansing blood;
And in simple faith to plunge me
'Neath the healing, cleansing flood!
slides.label: Verse 2

slides.text:
Jesus, Jesus, how I trust Him!
How I've proved Him o'er and o'er;
Jesus, Jesus, precious Jesus!
O for grace to trust Him more!
slides.label: Chorus

slides.text:
Yes, 'tis sweet to trust in Jesus,
Just from sin and self to cease;
Just from Jesus simply taking
Life and rest, and joy and peace.
slides.label: Verse 3

slides.text:
Jesus, Jesus, how I trust Him!
How I've proved Him o'er and o'er;
Jesus, Jesus, precious Jesus!
O for grace to trust Him more!
slides.label: Chorus

slides.text:
I'm so glad I learned to trust Thee,
Precious Jesus, Savior, friend;
And I know that Thou art with me,
Wilt be with me to the end.
slides.label: Verse 4

slides.text:
Jesus, Jesus, how I trust Him!
How I've proved Him o'er and o'er;
Jesus, Jesus, precious Jesus!
O for grace to trust Him more!
slides.label: Chorus

title: A Mighty Fortress Is Our God
author: Martin Luther, tr. Frederic H. Hedge

slides.text:
A mighty fortress is our God,
A bulwark never failing;
Our helper He, amid the flood
Of mortal ills prevailing:
For still our ancient foe
slides.label: Verse 1

slides.text:
Doth seek to work us woe;
His craft and power are great,
And, armed with cruel hate,
On earth is not his equal.
slides.label: Verse 1 (cont.)

slides.text:
Did we in our own strength confide,
Our striving would be losing;
Were not the right Man on our side,
The Man of God's own choosing:
Dost ask who that may be?
slides.label: Verse 2

slides.text:
Christ Jesus, it is He;
Lord Sabaoth, His name,
From age to age the same,
And He must win the battle.
slides.label: Verse 2 (cont.)

slides.text:
And though this world, with devils filled,
Should threaten to undo us,
We will not fear, for God hath willed
His truth to triumph through us:
The Prince of Darkness grim,
slides.label: Verse 3

slides.text:
We tremble not for him;
His rage we can endure,
For lo, his doom is sure,
One little word shall fell him.
slides.label: Verse 3 (cont.)

slides.text:
That word above all earthly powers,
No thanks to them, abideth;
The Spirit and the gifts are ours
Through Him who with us sideth:
Let goods and kindred go,
slides.label: Verse 4

slides.text:
This mortal life also;
The body they may kill:
God's truth abideth still,
His kingdom is forever.
slides.label: Verse 4 (cont.)

title: A Safe Stronghold Our God is Still
author: Martin Luther

slides.label: Verse 1

slides.text:
With force of arms we nothing can,
Full soon were we down-ridden;
But for us fights the proper Man,
Whom God Himself hath bidden.
Ask ye: Who is this same?
Christ Jesus is His name,
The Lord Sabaoth’s Son;
He, and no other one,
Shall conquer in the battle.
slides.label: Verse 2
Verse 3

slides.text:
God’s word, for all their craft and force,
One moment will not linger,
But, spite of hell, shall have its course;
’Tis written by His finger.
And though they take our life,
Goods, honour, children, wife,
Yet is their profit small:
These things shall vanish all;
The city of God remaineth.
slides.label: Verse 4
Verse 1
Verse 2

slides.text:
I need Thy presence every passing hour;
What but Thy grace can foil the tempter’s power?
Who like Thyself my guide and stay can be?
Through cloud and sunshine, O abide with me.
slides.label: Verse 3

slides.text:
I fear no foe, with Thee at hand to bless;
Ills have no weight, and tears no bitterness.
Where is death’s sting? Where, grave, thy victory? 
I triumph still, if Thou abide with me.
slides.label: Verse 4
Verse 5

title: All Creatures of our God and King
author: St. Francis of Assisi

slides.text:
All creatures of our God and King,
Lift up your voice and with us sing:
Hallelujah, hallelujah!
Thou burning sun with golden beam,
Thou silver moon with softer gleam:
slides.label: Verse 1

slides.text:
O praise Him, O praise Him,
Hallelujah, hallelujah, hallelujah!
slides.label: Chorus 1

slides.text:
Thou rushing wind that art so strong,
Ye clouds that sail in heaven along,
O praise Him, hallelujah!
Thou rising morn, in praise rejoice,
Ye lights of evening, find a voice:
slides.label: Verse 2

slides.text:
Thou flowing water, pure and clear,
Make music for thy Lord to hear,
Hallelujah, hallelujah!
Thou fire so masterful and bright,
That givest man both warmth and light:
slides.label: Verse 3

slides.text:
And all ye men of tender heart,
Forgiving others, take your part,
O sing ye, hallelujah!
Ye who long pain and sorrow bear,
Praise God and on Him cast your care:
slides.label: Verse 4

slides.text:
Let all things their Creator bless,
And worship Him in humbleness,
O praise Him, hallelujah!
Praise, praise the Father, praise the Son,
And praise the Spirit, Three-in-One:
slides.label: Verse 5

title: All Glory, Laud, and Honor
author: Theodulph of Orleans, tr. John M. Neale

slides.text:
All glory, laud and honor,
To Thee, Redeemer, King,
To whom the lips of children
Made sweet hosannas ring.
slides.label: Chorus

slides.text:
Thou art the King of Israel,
Thou David's royal Son,
Who in the Lord's name comest,
The King and Blessèd One.
slides.label: Verse 1

slides.text:
All glory, laud and honor,
To Thee, Redeemer, King,
To whom the lips of children
Made sweet hosannas ring.
slides.label: Chorus

slides.text:
The company of angels
Are praising Thee on high,
And mortal men and all things
Created make reply.
slides.label: Verse 2

slides.text:
All glory, laud and honor,
To Thee, Redeemer, King,
To whom the lips of children
Made sweet hosannas ring.
slides.label: Chorus

slides.text:
The people of the Hebrews
With palms before Thee went;
Our prayer and praise and anthems
Before Thee we present.
slides.label: Verse 3

slides.text:
All glory, laud and honor,
To Thee, Redeemer, King,
To whom the lips of children
Made sweet hosannas ring.
slides.label: Chorus

slides.text:
To Thee, before Thy passion,
They sang their hymns of praise;
To Thee, now high exalted,
Our melody we raise.
slides.label: Verse 4

slides.text:
All glory, laud and honor,
To Thee, Redeemer, King,
To whom the lips of children
Made sweet hosannas ring.
slides.label: Chorus

slides.text:
Thou didst accept their praises;
Accept the prayers we bring,
Who in all good delightest,
Thou good and gracious King.
slides.label: Verse 5

slides.text:
All glory, laud and honor,
To Thee, Redeemer, King,
To whom the lips of children
Made sweet hosannas ring.
slides.label: Chorus

slides.text:
Thy sorrow and Thy triumph
Grant us, O Christ, to share,
That to the holy city
Together we may fare.
slides.label: Verse 6

slides.text:
All glory, laud and honor,
To Thee, Redeemer, King,
To whom the lips of children
Made sweet hosannas ring.
slides.label: Chorus

slides.text:
For homage may we bring Thee
Our victory o'er the foe,
That in the Conqueror's triumph
This strain may ever flow.
slides.label: Verse 7

slides.text:
All glory, laud and honor,
To Thee, Redeemer, King,
To whom the lips of children
Made sweet hosannas ring.
slides.label: Chorus

title: All Hail the Power of Jesus Name
author: Edward Perronet

slides.text:
All hail the power of Jesus' name!
Let angels prostrate fall;
Bring forth the royal diadem,
And crown Him Lord of all.
slides.label: Verse 1

slides.text:
Crown Him, ye martyrs of your God,
Who from His altar call;
Extol Him in whose path ye trod,
And crown Him Lord of all.
slides.label: Verse 2

slides.text:
Ye seed of Israel’s chosen race,
Ye ransomed of the fall,
Hail Him who saves you by His grace,
And crown Him Lord of all.
slides.label: Verse 3

slides.text:
Sinners, whose love can ne’er forget
The wormwood and the gall,
Go, spread your trophies at His feet,
And crown Him Lord of all.
slides.label: Verse 4

slides.text:
Let every kindred, every tribe
On this terrestrial ball,
To Him all majesty ascribe,
And crown Him Lord of all.
slides.label: Verse 5

slides.text:
O that, with yonder sacred throng,
We at His feet may fall,
Join in the everlasting song,
And crown Him Lord of all!
slides.label: Verse 6

title: All People That on Earth Do Dwell
author: William Kethe

slides.text:
All people that on earth do dwell,
Sing to the Lord with cheerful voice;
Him serve with mirth, His praise forthtell,
Come ye before Him and rejoice.
slides.label: Verse 1

slides.text:
Know that the Lord is God indeed,
Without our aid He did us make:
We are His flock, He doth us feed,
And for His sheep He doth us take.
slides.label: Verse 2

slides.text:
O enter then His gates with praise,
Approach with joy His courts unto:
Praise, laud, and bless His name always,
For it is seemly so to do.
slides.label: Verse 3
Verse 4

slides.text:
Praise God from whom all blessings flow,
Praise Him all creatures here below,
Praise Him above, ye heavenly hosts;
Praise Father, Son and Holy Ghost.
slides.label: Verse 5

title: All the Way My Saviour Leads Me
author: Fanny Crosby

slides.text:
All the way my saviour leads me,
What have I to ask beside?
Can I doubt His tender mercy,
Who through life has been my guide?
Heavenly peace, divinest comfort,
Here by faith in Him to dwell,
For I know whate’er befall me,
Jesus doeth all things well.
slides.label: Verse 1

slides.text:
All the way my Saviour leads me,
Cheers each winding path I tread.
Gives me grace for every trial,
Feeds me with the Living Bread.
Though my weary steps may falter
And my soul athirst may be,
Gushing from a Rock before me,
Lo! a spring of joy I see.
slides.label: Verse 2

slides.text:
And all the way my Saviour leads me,
Oh, the fullness of His love.
Perfect rest to me is promised
In my Father’s house above.
And when my spirit clothed immortal
Wings its flight to realms of day,
This my song through endless ages,
Jesus led me all the way.
slides.label: Verse 3

slides.text:
All things bright and beautiful,
All creatures great and small,
All things wise and wonderful,
The Lord God made them all.
slides.label: Verse 1

slides.text:
Each little flower that opens,
Each little bird that sings,
He made their glowing colours,
He made their tiny wings.
slides.label: Verse 2

slides.text:
The purple-headed mountain,
The river running by,
The sunset, and the morning
That brightens up the sky.
slides.label: Verse 3

slides.text:
The cold wind in the winter,
The pleasant summer sun,
The ripe fruits in the garden,
He made them every one.
slides.label: Verse 4

slides.text:
He gave us eyes to see them,
And lips that we might tell
How great is God Almighty,
Who has made all things well.
slides.label: Verse 5

title: Am I a Soldier of the Cross
author: Isaac Watts

slides.text:
Am I a soldier of the cross,
A follower of the Lamb,
And shall I fear to own His cause,
Or blush to speak His name?
slides.label: Verse 1

slides.text:
Must I be carried to the skies
On flowery beds of ease,
While others fought to win the prize,
And sailed through bloody seas?
slides.label: Verse 2

slides.text:
Are there no foes for me to face?
Must I not stem the flood?
Is this vile world a friend to grace,
To help me on to God?
slides.label: Verse 3

slides.text:
Sure I must fight if I would reign;
Increase my courage, Lord.
I'll bear the toil, endure the pain,
Supported by Thy Word.
slides.label: Verse 4

slides.text:
Thy saints in all this glorious war
Shall conquer, though they die;
They see the triumph from afar,
By faith's discerning eye.
slides.label: Verse 5

slides.text:
When that illustrious day shall rise,
And all Thy armies shine
In robes of victory through the skies,
The glory shall be Thine.
slides.label: Verse 6

slides.text:
Amazing Grace! how sweet the sound
That saved a wretch like me;
I once was lost, but now am found,
Was blind, but now I see.
slides.label: Verse 1

slides.text:
’Twas grace that taught my heart to fear,
And grace my fears relieved;
How precious did that grace appear,
The hour I first believed!
slides.label: Verse 2

slides.text:
Through many dangers, toils and snares
I have already come;
’Tis grace that brought me safe thus far,
And grace will lead me home.
slides.label: Verse 3

slides.text:
The Lord has promised good to me,
His word my hope secures;
He will my shield and portion be
As long as life endures.
slides.label: Verse 4

slides.text:
Yes, when this heart and flesh shall fail,
And mortal life shall cease,
I shall possess within the veil
A life of joy and peace.
slides.label: Verse 5

slides.text:
When we’ve been there a thousand years,
Bright shining as the sun,
We’ve no less days to sing God’s praise
Than when we first begun.
slides.label: Verse 6

slides.text:
And can it be that I should gain
An interest in the Saviour’s blood?
Died He for me, who caused His pain?
For me, who Him to death pursued?
Amazing love! how can it be
That Thou, my God, shouldst die for me?
Amazing love! how can it be
That Thou, my God, shouldst die for me?
slides.label: Verse 1

slides.text:
’Tis mystery all! The Immortal dies:
Who can explore His strange design?
In vain the first-born seraph tries
To sound the depths of love divine!
’Tis mercy all! let earth adore,
Let angel minds inquire no more.
Amazing love! how can it be
That Thou, my God, shouldst die for me?
slides.label: Verse 2

slides.text:
He left His Father’s throne above,
So free, so infinite His grace;
Emptied Himself of all but love,
And bled for Adam’s helpless race.
‘Tis mercy all, immense and free;
For, O my God, it found out me.
Amazing love! how can it be
That Thou, my God, shouldst die for me?
slides.label: Verse 3
Verse 4

slides.text:
No condemnation now I dread;
Jesus, and all in Him, is mine!
Alive in Him, my living Head,
And clothed in righteousness divine,
Bold I approach the eternal throne,
And claim the crown, through Christ my own. 
Amazing love! how can it be
That Thou, my God, shouldst die for me?
slides.label: Verse 5

slides.text:
Angel voices ever singing
Round Thy throne of light,
Angel harps forever ringing,
Rest not day nor night;
slides.label: Verse 1

slides.text:
Thousands only live to bless Thee,
And confess Thee
Lord of might.
slides.label: Verse 2

slides.text:
Thou who art beyond the farthest
Mortal eye can scan,
Can it be that Thou regardest
Songs of sinful man?
slides.label: Verse 3

slides.text:
Can we know that Thou art near us
And wilt hear us?
Yes, we can.
slides.label: Verse 4
Verse 5

slides.text:
Craftsman’s art and music’s measure
For Thy pleasure
All combine.
slides.label: Verse 6

slides.text:
In Thy house, great God, we offer
Of Thine own to Thee,
And for Thine acceptance proffer,
All unworthily,
slides.label: Verse 7

slides.text:
Hearts and minds and hands and voices
In our choicest
Psalmody.
slides.label: Verse 8

slides.text:
Honour, glory, might, and merit
Thine shall ever be,
Father, Son, and Holy Spirit,
Blessed Trinity.
slides.label: Verse 9

slides.text:
Of the best that Thou hast given
Earth and heaven
Render Thee.
slides.label: Verse 10

title: Angels From the Realms of Glory
author: James Montgomery

slides.text:
Angels, from the realms of Glory,
Wing your flight o’er all the earth;
Ye who sang creation’s story,
Now proclaim Messiah’s birth:
slides.label: Verse 1

slides.text:
Come and worship
Christ, the new-born King.
Come and worship
Worship Christ, the new-born King.
slides.label: Verse 2

slides.text:
Shepherds, in the field abiding,
Watching o’er your flocks by night,
God with man is now residing,
Yonder shines the infant-light:
slides.label: Verse 3

slides.text:
Sages, leave your contemplations,
Brighter visions beam afar;
Seek the great desire of nations,
Ye have seen His natal star:
slides.label: Verse 4

slides.text:
Saints, before the altar bending,
Watching long in hope and fear,
Suddenly the Lord descending
In His temple shall appear:
slides.label: Verse 5

title: Angels We Have Heard on High
author: Traditional French carol, tr. James Chadwick

slides.text:
Angels we have heard on high
Sweetly singing o'er the plains,
And the mountains in reply
Echoing their joyous strains.
slides.label: Verse 1

slides.text:
Gloria, in excelsis Deo!
Gloria, in excelsis Deo!
slides.label: Chorus

slides.text:
Shepherds, why this jubilee?
Why your joyous strains prolong?
What the gladsome tidings be
Which inspire your heav'nly song?
slides.label: Verse 2

slides.text:
Gloria, in excelsis Deo!
Gloria, in excelsis Deo!
slides.label: Chorus

slides.text:
Come to Bethlehem and see
Christ whose birth the angels sing;
Come, adore on bended knee,
Christ the Lord, the newborn King.
slides.label: Verse 3

slides.text:
Gloria, in excelsis Deo!
Gloria, in excelsis Deo!
slides.label: Chorus

slides.text:
See Him in a manger laid,
Whom the choirs of angels praise;
Mary, Joseph, lend your aid,
While our hearts in love we raise.
slides.label: Verse 4

slides.text:
Gloria, in excelsis Deo!
Gloria, in excelsis Deo!
slides.label: Chorus

slides.text:
Arise, my soul, arise;
Shake off thy guilty fears;
The bleeding sacrifice
In my behalf appears:
Before the throne my surety stands,
Before the throne my surety stands,
My name is written on His hands.
slides.label: Verse 1

slides.text:
He ever lives above,
For me to intercede;
His all redeeming love,
His precious blood, to plead:
His blood atoned for all our race,
His blood atoned for all our race,
And sprinkles now the throne of grace.
slides.label: Verse 2
Verse 3

slides.text:
The Father hears Him pray,
His dear anointed One;
He cannot turn away,
The presence of His Son;
His Spirit answers to the blood,
His Spirit answers to the blood,
And tells me I am born of God.
slides.label: Verse 4
Verse 5

slides.text:
As with gladness men of old
Did the guiding star behold;
As with joy they hailed its light,
Leading onward, beaming bright,
So, most gracious God, may we
Evermore be led by Thee.
slides.label: Verse 1

slides.text:
As with joyful steps they sped,
Saviour, to Thy lowly bed,
There to bend the knee before
Thee whom heaven and earth adore,
So may we with willing feet
Ever seek Thy mercy-seat.
As they offered gifts most rare
At Thy cradle rude and bare,
So may we with holy joy,
Pure, and free from sin’s alloy,
All our costliest treasures bring,
Christ, to Thee, our heavenly King.
slides.label: Verse 2

slides.text:
Holy Jesus, every day
Keep us in the narrow way;
And, when earthly things are past,
Bring our ransomed souls at last
Where they need no star to guide,
Where no clouds Thy glory hide.
slides.label: Verse 3

slides.text:
In the heavenly country bright
Need they no created light;
Thou its light, its joy, its crown,
Thou its sun, which goes not down.
There forever may we sing
Hallelujahs to our King.
slides.label: Verse 4

slides.text:
At the name of Jesus,
Every knee shall bow,
Every tongue confess Him
King of glory now;
’Tis the Father’s pleasure
We should call Him Lord,
Who from the beginning
Was the mighty Word.
slides.label: Verse 1

slides.text:
Humbled for a season,
To receive a name
From the lips of sinners
Unto whom He came;
Faithfully He bore it
Spotless to the last,
Brought it back victorious,
When from death He passed.
slides.label: Verse 2

slides.text:
Bore it up triumphant
With its human light,
Through all ranks of creatures
To the central height,
To the throne of Godhead,
To the Father’s breast,
Filled it with the glory
Of that perfect rest.
slides.label: Verse 3

slides.text:
In your hearts enthrone Him;
There let Him subdue
All that is not holy,
All that is not true;
Crown Him as your Captain
In temptation’s hour,
Let His will enfold you
In its light and power.
slides.label: Verse 4

slides.text:
Brothers, this Lord Jesus
Shall return again,
With His Father’s glory,
With His angel-train;
For all wreaths of empire
Meet upon His brow,
And our hearts confess Him
King of glory now.
slides.label: Verse 5

title: Awake, My Soul, and with the Sun
author: Thomas Ken

slides.text:
Awake, my soul, and with the sun
Thy daily stage of duty run;
Shake off dull sloth, and joyful rise,
To pay thy morning sacrifice.
slides.label: Verse 1

slides.text:
Thy precious time misspent, redeem,
Each present day thy last esteem,
Improve thy talent with due care;
For the great day thyself prepare.
slides.label: Verse 2

slides.text:
By influence of the Light divine
Let thy own light to others shine.
Reflect all Heaven's propitious ways
In ardent love, and cheerful praise.
slides.label: Verse 3
Verse 4

slides.text:
Wake, and lift up thyself, my heart,
And with the angels bear thy part,
Who all night long unwearied sing
High praise to the eternal King.
slides.label: Verse 5

slides.text:
All praise to Thee, who safe has kept
And hast refreshed me while I slept
Grant, Lord, when I from death shall wake
I may of endless light partake.
slides.label: Verse 6

slides.text:
Heav'n is, dear Lord, where'er Thou art,
O never then from me depart;
For to my soul 'tis hell to be
But for one moment void of Thee.
slides.label: Verse 7

slides.text:
Lord, I my vows to Thee renew;
Disperse my sins as morning dew.
Guard my first springs of thought and will,
And with Thyself my spirit fill.
slides.label: Verse 8

slides.text:
Direct, control, suggest, this day,
All I design, or do, or say,
That all my powers, with all their might,
In Thy sole glory may unite.
slides.label: Verse 9

slides.text:
I would not wake nor rise again
And Heav'n itself I would disdain,
Wert Thou not there to be enjoyed,
And I in hymns to be employed.
slides.label: Verse 10
Verse 11

title: Away in a Manger
author: Author Unknown, J. T. McFarland

slides.text:
Away in a manger,
No crib for a bed,
The little Lord Jesus
Laid down His sweet head;
The stars in the bright sky
Looked down where He lay;
The little Lord Jesus
Asleep on the hay.
slides.label: Verse 1

slides.text:
The cattle are lowing, the Baby awakes,
But little Lord Jesus, no crying He makes:
I love You, Lord Jesus! Look down from the sky
And stay by my side until morning is nigh.
slides.label: Verse 2

slides.text:
Be near me, Lord Jesus: I ask You to stay
Close by me forever and love me, I pray;
Bless all the dear children in Your tender care,
And fit us for heaven to live with You there.
slides.label: Verse 3

basis: anonymous text (1885-87); music by J. T. McFarland (1887)

title: Be Known to us in Breaking Bread
author: James Montgomery

slides.text:
Be known to is breaking bread,
But do not then depart;
Saviour, abide with us, and spread
Thy table in our heart.
slides.label: Verse 1

slides.text:
There sup with us in love divine;
Thy body and Thy blood,
That living bread, that heavenly wine,
Be our immortal food.
slides.label: Verse 2

slides.text:
We would not live by bread alone,
But by Thy word of grace,
In strength of which we travel on
To our abiding place.
slides.label: Verse 3

title: Be Still, My Soul
author: Katharina von Schlegel, tr. Jane L. Borthwick

slides.text:
Be still, my soul: the Lord is on thy side.
Bear patiently the cross of grief or pain.
Leave to thy God to order and provide;
In every change, He faithful will remain.
Be still, my soul: thy best, thy heavenly friend
Through thorny ways leads to a joyful end.
slides.label: Verse 1

slides.text:
Be still, my soul: thy God doth undertake
To guide the future, as He has the past.
Thy hope, thy confidence let nothing shake;
All now mysterious shall be bright at last.
Be still, my soul: the waves and winds still know
His voice who ruled them while He dwelt below.
slides.label: Verse 2

slides.text:
Be still, my soul: when dearest friends depart,
And all is darkened in the vale of tears,
Then shalt thou better know His love, His heart,
Who comes to soothe thy sorrow and thy fears.
Be still, my soul: thy Jesus can repay
From His on fullness all He takes away.
slides.label: Verse 3

slides.text:
Be still, my soul: the hour is hastening on
When we shall be forever with the Lord.
When disappointment, grief and fear are gone,
Sorrow forgot, love's purest joys restored.
Be still, my soul: when change and tears are past
All safe and blessèd we shall meet at last.
slides.label: Verse 4

slides.text:
Be still, my soul: begin the song of praise
On earth, believing, to Thy Lord on high;
Acknowledge Him in all thy words and ways,
So shall He view thee with a well-pleased eye.
Be still, my soul: the Sun of life divine
Through passing clouds shall but more brightly shine.
slides.label: Verse 5

title: Be Thou my Vision
author: Mary E. Byrne, Eleanor H. Hull

slides.text:
Be Thou my vision, O Lord of my heart,
Be all else but naught to me, save that Thou art;
Be Thou my best thought in the day and the night,
Both waking and sleeping, Thy presence my light.
slides.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
Verse 3

slides.text:
Riches I need not, nor man’s empty praise:
Be Thou mine inheritance now and always;
Be Thou and Thou only the first in my heart:
O Sovereign of heaven, my treasure Thou art.
slides.label: Verse 4

slides.text:
High King of heaven, Thou heaven’s bright Sun,
O grant me its joys after victory is won;
Great Heart of my own heart, whatever befall,
Still be Thou my vision, O Ruler of all.
slides.label: Verse 5

title: Before the Throne of God Above
author: Charitie L. Bancroft

slides.text:
Before the throne of God above,
I have a strong, a perfect plea,
A great High Priest whose name is Love,
Who ever lives and pleads for me.
My name is graven on His hands,
My name is written on His heart;
I know that while in heaven He stands 
No tongue can bid me thence depart,
No tongue can bid me thence depart.
slides.label: Verse 1

slides.text:
When Satan tempts me to despair,
And tells me of the guilt within,
Upward I look and see Him there 
Who made an end to all my sin.
Because the sinless Saviour died,
My sinful soul is counted free;
For God the Just is satisfied
To look on Him and pardon me,
To look on Him and pardon me.
slides.label: Verse 2

slides.text:
Behold Him there! The risen Lamb,
My perfect, spotless righteousness;
The great unchangeable I AM,
The King of glory and of grace!
One with Himself I cannot die,
My soul is purchased with His blood;
My life is hid with Christ on high,
With Christ, my Saviour and my God,
With Christ my Saviour and my God.
slides.label: Verse 3

title: Behold the Servant of the Lord
author: Charles Wesley

slides.text:
Behold the servant of the Lord:
I wait Thy guiding eye to feel,
To hear and keep Thy every word,
To prove and do Thy perfect will;
Joyful from my own works to cease,
Glad to fulfil all righteousness.
slides.label: Verse 1

slides.text:
Me if Thy grace vouchsafe to use,
Meanest of all Thy creatures, me.
The deed, the time, the manner choose:
Let all my fruit be found of Thee.
Let all my works in Thee be wrought,
By Thee to full perfection brought.
slides.label: Verse 2

slides.text:
My every weak though good design
O’errule or change, as seems Thee meet:
Jesus, let all my work be Thine –
Thy work, O Lord, is all complete,
And pleasing in Thy Father’s sight;
Thou only hast done all things right.
slides.label: Verse 3
Verse 4

slides.text:
Beneanth the cross of Jesus
I fain would take my stand,
The shadow of a mighty rock
Within a weary land;
A home within the wilderness,
A rest upon the way,
From the burning of the noontide heat,
And the burden of the day.
slides.label: Verse 1

slides.text:
O safe and happy shelter!
O refuge tried and sweet!
O trysting place where heaven’s love
And heaven’s justice meet!
As to the holy patriarch
That wondrous dream was given,
So seems my Saviour’s cross to me
A ladder up to heaven.
slides.label: Verse 2

slides.text:
There lies, beneath its shadow,
But on the farther side,
The darkness of an awful grave
That gapes both deep and wide;
And there between us stands the cross,
Two arms outstretched to save;
Like a watchman set to guard the way
From that eternal grave.
slides.label: Verse 3

slides.text:
Upon that cross of Jesus
Mine eye at times can see
The very dying form of One
Who suffered there for me;
And from my smitten heart, with tears,
Two wonders I confess—
The wonders of His glorious love,
And my own worthlessness.
slides.label: Verse 4

slides.text:
I take, O cross, thy shadow,
For my abiding place;
I ask no other sunshine than
The sunshine of His face;
Content to let the world go by,
To know no gain nor loss—
My sinful self my only shame,
My glory all the cross.
slides.label: Verse 5

slides.text:
Blessed assurance, Jesus is mine:
O what a foretaste of glory divine!
Heir of salvation, purchase of God;
Born of His Spirit, washed in His blood.
slides.label: Verse 1

slides.text:
This is my story, this is my song,
Praising my Saviour all the day long.
This is my story, this is my song,
Praising my Saviour all the day long.
slides.label: Verse 2

slides.text:
Perfect submission, perfect delight,
Visions of rapture burst on my sight;
Angels descending bring from above
Echoes of mercy, whispers of love.
slides.label: Verse 3

slides.text:
Perfect submission, all is at rest,
I in my Saviour am happy and blessed;
Watching and waiting, looking above,
Filled with His goodness, lost in His love.
slides.label: Verse 4

slides.text:
Blest be the tie that binds
Our hearts in Christian love;
The fellowship of kindred minds
Is like to that above.
slides.label: Verse 1

slides.text:
Before our Father’s throne
We pour our ardent prayers;
Our fears, our hopes, our aims are one,
Our comforts and our cares.
slides.label: Verse 2

slides.text:
We share our mutual woes,
Our mutual burdens bear,
And often for each other flows
The sympathising tear.
slides.label: Verse 3

slides.text:
When for a while we part,
This thought will soothe our pain,
That we shall still be joined in heart,
And hope to meet again.
slides.label: Verse 4

slides.text:
This glorious hope revives
Our courage by the way,
While each in expectation lives,
And longs to see the day.
slides.label: Verse 5

slides.text:
From sorrow, toil and pain,
And sin we shall be free;
And perfect love and friendship reign
Through all eternity.
slides.label: Verse 6

title: Break Thou the Bread of Life
author: Mary A. Lathbury, Alexander Groves

slides.text:
Break thou the bread of Life,
Dear Lord, to me,
As Thou didst break the bread
Beside the sea;
slides.label: Verse 1

slides.text:
Beyond the sacred page
I seek Thee, Lord;
My spirit longs for Thee,
Thou Living Word.
slides.label: Verse 2

slides.text:
Thou art the Bread of Life,
O Lord, to me,
Thy holy Word the truth
That saveth me;
slides.label: Verse 3

slides.text:
Give me to eat and live
With Thee above;
Teach me to love Thy truth,
For Thou art love.
slides.label: Verse 4

slides.text:
O send Thy Spirit, Lord,
Now unto me,
That He may touch my eyes
And make me see;
slides.label: Verse 5

slides.text:
Show me the truth concealed
Within Thy Word,
And in Thy Book revealed,
I see Thee, Lord.
slides.label: Verse 6

slides.text:
Bless Thou the Bread of Life
To me, to me,
As Thou didst bless the loaves
By Galilee;
slides.label: Verse 7

slides.text:
Then shall all bondage cease,
All fetters fall,
And I shall find my peace,
My all in all.
slides.label: Verse 8

title: Breathe On Me, Breath of God
author: Edwin Hatch

slides.text:
Breathe on me, Breath of God,
Fill me with life anew;
That I may love what Thou dost love
And do what Thou wouldst do.
slides.label: Verse 1

slides.text:
Breathe on me, Breath of God,
Until my heart is pure;
Until my will is one with Thine
To do and to endure.
slides.label: Verse 2

slides.text:
Breathe on me, Breath of God,
Till I am wholly Thine;
Until this earthly part of me
Glows with Thy fire divine.
slides.label: Verse 3

slides.text:
Breathe on me, Breath of God,
So shall I never die,
But live with Thee the perfect life
Of Thine eternity.
slides.label: Verse 4

title: Brethren, We Have Met to Worship
author: George Atkins

slides.text:
Brethren, we have met to worship
And adore the Lord our God;
Will you pray with all your power,
While we meet to preach His Word?
slides.label: Verse 1

slides.text:
All is vain unless the Spirit
Of the Holy One comes down;
Brethren, pray, and holy manna
Will be showered all around.
slides.label: Verse 2
Verse 3

slides.text:
See our fathers and our mothers,
And our children sinking down;
Brethren, pray and holy manna
Will be showered all around.
slides.label: Verse 4

slides.text:
Brethren, there are poor backsliders,
Who were once near Heaven's door;
But they have betrayed the Savior,
And are worse than e'en before.
slides.label: Verse 5

slides.text:
Yet the Savior offers pardon,
If they will lament their wound;
Brethren, pray, and holy manna
Will be showered all around.
slides.label: Verse 6
Verse 7
Verse 8

title: Christ the Lord is Risen Today
author: Charles Wesley

slides.text:
Christ the Lord is Risen today: Hallelujah!
Sons of men and angels say: Hallelujah!
Raise your joys and triumphs high: Hallelujah!
Sing, ye heavens, and earth reply: Hallelujah!
slides.label: Verse 1

slides.text:
Love’s redeeming work is done: Hallelujah!
Fought the fight, the battle won: Hallelujah!
Vain the stone, the watch, the seal: Hallelujah!
Christ hath burst the gates of hell: Hallelujah!
slides.label: Verse 2

slides.text:
Lives again our glorious King: Hallelujah!
Where, O death, is now thy sting? Hallelujah!
Once He died, our souls to save: Hallelujah!
Where thy victory, O grave? Hallelujah!
slides.label: Verse 3

slides.text:
Soar we now where Christ hath led: Hallelujah!
Following our exalted Head: Hallelujah!
Made like Him, like Him we rise: Hallelujah!
Ours the cross, the grave, the skies: Hallelujah!
slides.label: Verse 4

slides.text:
Hail the Lord of earth and heaven: Hallelujah!
Praise to Thee by both be given: Hallelujah!
Thee we greet, in triumph sing: Hallelujah!
Hail our resurrected King: Hallelujah!
slides.label: Verse 5

title: Christ, Whose Glory Fills the Skies
author: Charles Wesley

slides.text:
Christ, whose glory fills the skies,
Christ, the true, the only light,
Sun of righteousness, arise,
Triumph o'er the shades of night:
Day-spring from on high, be near;
Day-star in my heart appear.
slides.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
Verse 3
Verse 1

slides.text:
Then to the watchful shepherds it was told,
Who heard the angelic herald’s voice ‘Behold,
I bring good tidings of a Saviour’s birth
To you and all the nations upon earth:
This day hath God fulfilled His promised word,
This day is born a Saviour, Christ the Lord.’
slides.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
Verse 4

slides.text:
Then may we hope, the angelic hosts among,
To sing, redeemed, a glad triumphant song:
He that was born upon this joyful day
Around us all His glory shall display;
Saved by His love, incessant we shall sing
Eternal praise to heaven’s almighty King.
slides.label: Verse 5

slides.text:
Come down, O Love Divine,
Seek Thou this soul of mine
And visit it with Thine own ardour glowing;
O Comforter, draw near,
Within my heart appear,
And kindle it, Thy holy flame bestowing.
slides.label: Verse 1

slides.text:
O let it freely burn,
Till earthly passions turn
To dust and ashes, in its heat consuming;
And let Thy glorious light
Shine ever on my sight,
And clothe me round, the while my path illuming.
slides.label: Verse 2

slides.text:
Let holy charity
Mine outward vesture be,
And lowliness become mine inner clothing;
True lowliness of heart,
Which takes the humbler part,
And o'er its own shortcomings weeps with loathing.
slides.label: Verse 3

slides.text:
And so the yearning strong,
With which the soul will long,
Shall far outpass the power of human telling;
For none can guess its grace,
Till he become the place
Wherein the Holy Spirit makes His dwelling.
slides.label: Verse 4

title: Come Let Us Join Our Cheerful Songs
author: Isaac Watts

slides.text:
Come, let us join our cheerful songs,
With angels round the throne;
Ten thousand thousand are their tongues,
But all their joys are one.
‘Worthy the Lamb that died,’ they cry,
‘To be exalted thus.’
‘Worthy the Lamb,’ our lips reply,
‘For He was slain for us.’
slides.label: Verse 1

slides.text:
Jesus is worthy to receive
Honour and power divine:
And blessings, more than we can give,
Be, Lord, forever Thine.
slides.label: Verse 2

slides.text:
Let all that dwell above the sky,
And air, and earth, and seas,
Conspire to lift Thy glories high,
And speak Thine endless praise.
slides.label: Verse 3

slides.text:
The whole creation join in one
To bless the sacred name
Of Him that sits upon the throne
And to adore the Lamb.
slides.label: Verse 4

title: Come Let Us Sing of a Wonderful Love
author: Robert Walmsley

slides.text:
Come, let us sing of a wonderful love,
Tender and true;
Out of the heart of the Father above,
Streaming to me and to you:
Wonderful love
Dwells in the heart of the Father above.
slides.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
Verse 3

slides.text:
Come to my heart, O Thou wonderful love,
Come and abide,
Lifting my life, till it rises above
Envy and falsehood and pride,
Seeking to be
Lowly and humble, a learner of Thee.
slides.label: Verse 4

slides.text:
Come, ye thankful people, come,
Raise the song of harvest home!
All is safely gathered in
Ere the winter storms begin;
slides.label: Verse 1

slides.text:
God, our Maker, doth provide
For our needs to be supplied;
Come to God’s own temple, come,
Raise the song of harvest-home.
slides.label: Verse 2
Verse 3

slides.text:
First the blade, and then the ear,
Then the full corn shall appear:
Lord of harvest, grant that we
Wholesome grain and pure may be.
slides.label: Verse 4

slides.text:
For the Lord our God shall come
And shall take His harvest home,
From His field shall in that day
All offences purge away,
slides.label: Verse 5

slides.text:
Give His angels charge at last
In the fire the tares to cast,
But the fruitful ears to store
In His garner evermore.
slides.label: Verse 6
Verse 7

slides.text:
There, forever purified,
In Thy garner to abide:
Come, with all Thine angels, come,
Raise the glorious harvest-home.
slides.label: Verse 8

slides.text:
Come, Holy Spirit, heav'nly Dove,
With all Thy quick'ning powers;
Kindle a flame of sacred love
In these cold hearts of ours.
slides.label: Verse 1

slides.text:
Look how we grovel here below,
Fond of these trifling toys;
Our souls can neither fly nor go
To reach eternal joys.
slides.label: Verse 2

slides.text:
In vain we tune our formal songs,
In vain we strive to rise;
Hosannas languish on our tongues,
And our devotion dies.
slides.label: Verse 3

slides.text:
Dear Lord! and shall we ever live
At this poor dying rate?
Our love so faint, so cold to Thee,
And Thine to us so great?
slides.label: Verse 4

slides.text:
Come, Holy Spirit, heav'nly Dove,
With all Thy quick'ning powers;
Come, shed abroad the Savior's love
And that shall kindle ours.
slides.label: Verse 5

title: Come, Thou Fount of Every Blessing
author: Robert Robinson

slides.text:
Come, Thou fount of every blessing,
Tune my heart to sing Thy grace;
Streams of mercy, never ceasing,
Call for songs of loudest praise.
Teach me some melodious sonnet,
Sung by flaming tongues above.
Praise the mount! I'm fixed upon it,
Mount of Thy redeeming love.
slides.label: Verse 1
Verse 2

slides.text:
Jesus sought me when a stranger,
Wandering from the fold of God;
He, to rescue me from danger,
Interposed His precious blood;
How His kindness yet pursues me
Mortal tongue can never tell,
Clothed in flesh, till death shall loose me
I cannot proclaim it well.
slides.label: Verse 3

slides.text:
O to grace how great a debtor
Daily I'm constrained to be!
Let Thy goodness, like a fetter,
Bind my wandering heart to Thee.
Prone to wander, Lord, I feel it,
Prone to leave the God I love;
Here's my heart, O take and seal it,
Seal it for Thy courts above.
slides.label: Verse 4
Verse 5

title: Come, Ye Faithful, Raise the Strain
author: John of Damascus, tr. John M. Neale

slides.text:
Come, ye faithful, raise the strain
Of triumphant gladness;
God hath brought forth Israel
Into joy from sadness;
Loosed from Pharaoh's bitter yoke
Jacob's sons and daughters,
Led them with unmoistened foot
Through the Red Sea waters.
slides.label: Verse 1

slides.text:
'Tis the spring of souls today;
Christ has burst His prison,
And from three days' sleep in death
As a sun hath risen;
All the winter of our sins,
Long and dark, is flying
From His light, to whom we give
Laud and praise undying.
slides.label: Verse 2

slides.text:
Now the queen of seasons, bright
With the day of splendor,
With the royal feast of feasts,
Comes its joy to render;
Comes to glad Jerusalem,
Who with true affection
Welcomes in unwearied strains
Jesus' resurrection.
slides.label: Verse 3

slides.text:
Neither might the gates of death,
Nor the tomb's dark portal,
Nor the watchers, nor the seal
Hold Thee as a mortal;
But today amidst the twelve
Thou didst stand, bestowing
That Thy peace which evermore
Passeth human knowing.
slides.label: Verse 4

slides.text:
Alleluia! now we cry
To our king immortal,
Who, triumphant, burst the bars
Of the tomb's dark portal;
Alleluia! with the Son,
God the Father praising,
Alleluia! yet again
To the Spirit raising.
slides.label: Verse 5

slides.text:
When upon life's billows
You are tempest tossed,
When you are discouraged,
Thinking all is lost,
Count your many blessings,
Name them one by one,
And it will surprise you
What the Lord hath done.
slides.label: Verse 1

slides.text:
Count your blessings,
Name them one by one,
Count your blessings,
See what God hath done!
Count your blessings,
Name them one by one,
And it will surprise you
What the Lord hath done.
slides.label: Chorus

slides.text:
Are you ever burdened
With a load of care?
Does the cross seem heavy
You are called to bear?
Count your many blessings,
Every doubt will fly,
And you will keep singing
As the days go by.
slides.label: Verse 2

slides.text:
Count your blessings,
Name them one by one,
Count your blessings,
See what God hath done!
Count your blessings,
Name them one by one,
And it will surprise you
What the Lord hath done.
slides.label: Chorus

slides.text:
When you look at others
With their lands and gold,
Think that Christ has promised
You His wealth untold;
Count your many blessings.
Wealth can never buy
Your reward in Heaven,
Nor your home on high.
slides.label: Verse 3

slides.text:
Count your blessings,
Name them one by one,
Count your blessings,
See what God hath done!
Count your blessings,
Name them one by one,
And it will surprise you
What the Lord hath done.
slides.label: Chorus

slides.text:
So, amid the conflict
Whether great or small,
Do not be disheartened,
God is over all;
Count your many blessings,
Angels will attend,
Help and comfort give you
To your journey's end.
slides.label: Verse 4

slides.text:
Count your blessings,
Name them one by one,
Count your blessings,
See what God hath done!
Count your blessings,
Name them one by one,
And it will surprise you
What the Lord hath done.
slides.label: Chorus

slides.text:
Crown Him with many crowns,
The Lamb upon His throne;
Hark, how the heavenly anthem drowns
All music but its own!
Awake, my soul, and sing
Of Him who died for thee,
And hail Him as thy matchless King
Through all eternity.
slides.label: Verse 1

slides.text:
Crown Him the Lord of life,
Who triumphed o’er the grave
And rose victorious in the strife
For those He came to save:
His glories now we sing,
Who died and rose on high,
Who died eternal life to bring
And lives that death may die.
slides.label: Verse 2

slides.text:
Crown Him the Lord of love;
Behold His hands and side,
Those wounds yet visible above
In beauty glorified:
No angel in the sky
Can fully bear that sight,
But downward bends His burning eye
At mysteries so bright.
slides.label: Verse 3

slides.text:
Crown Him the Lord of peace,
Whose power a sceptre sways
From pole to pole, that wars may cease,
And all be prayer and praise:
His reign shall know no end,
And round His pierced feet
Fair flowers of paradise extend
Their fragrance ever sweet.
slides.label: Verse 4

slides.text:
Crown Him the Lord of years,
The Potentate of time,
Creator of the rolling spheres,
Ineffably sublime!
All hail, Redeemer, hail!
For Thou hast died for me;
Thy praise shall never, never fail
Throughout eternity.
slides.label: Verse 5

title: Dear Lord and Father of Mankind
author: John G. Whittier

slides.label: Verse 1

slides.text:
In simple trust like theirs who heard,
Beside the Syrian sea,
The gracious calling of the Lord,
Let us, like them, without a word
Rise up and follow Thee,
Rise up and follow Thee.
slides.label: Verse 2

slides.text:
O sabbath rest by Galilee!
O calm of hills above,
Where Jesus knelt to share with Thee
The silence of eternity,
Interpreted by love,
Interpreted by love.
slides.label: Verse 3

slides.text:
With that deep hush subduing all
Our words and works that drown
The tender whisper of Thy call,
As noiseless let Thy blessing fall
As fell Thy manna down,
As fell Thy manna down.
Drop Thy still dews of quietness,
Till all our strivings cease;
Take from our souls the strain and stress,
And let our ordered lives confess
The beauty of Thy peace,
The beauty of Thy peace.
slides.label: Verse 4
Verse 5

slides.text:
Eternal Father, strong to save,
Whose arm hath bound the restless wave,
Who bidd'st the mighty ocean deep
Its own appointed limits keep:
O hear us when we cry to Thee
For those in peril on the sea.
slides.label: Verse 1

slides.text:
O Christ, whose voice the waters heard,
And hushed their raging at Thy word,
Who walkedst on the foaming deep,
And calm amid the storm didst sleep:
O hear us when we cry to Thee
For those in peril on the sea.
slides.label: Verse 2

slides.text:
O Holy Spirit, who didst brood
Upon the waters dark and rude,
And bid their angry tumult cease,
And give, for wild confusion, peace:
O hear us when we cry to Thee
For those in peril on the sea.
slides.label: Verse 3

slides.text:
O Trinity of love and power,
Our brethren shield in danger's hour;
From rock and tempest, fire and foe,
Protect them wheresoe'er they go:
Thus evermore shall rise to Thee
Glad hymns of praise from land and sea.
slides.label: Verse 4

title: Fairest Lord Jesus
author: Anonymous (17th century German), tr. Joseph A. Seiss

slides.text:
Fairest Lord Jesus, Ruler of all nature,
O Thou of God and man the Son,
Thee will I cherish, Thee will I honor,
Thou, my soul's glory, joy and crown.
slides.label: Verse 1

slides.text:
Fair are the meadows, fairer still the woodlands,
Robed in the blooming garb of spring;
Jesus is fairer, Jesus is purer,
Who makes the woeful heart to sing.
slides.label: Verse 2

slides.text:
Fair is the sunshine, fairer still the moonlight,
And all the twinkling starry host;
Jesus shines brighter, Jesus shines purer
Than all the angels Heav'n can boast.
slides.label: Verse 3

slides.text:
All fairest beauty, heavenly and earthly,
Wondrously, Jesus, is found in Thee;
None can be nearer, fairer or dearer,
Than Thou, my Savior, art to me.
slides.label: Verse 4

slides.text:
Beautiful Savior! Lord of all the nations!
Son of God and Son of Man!
Glory and honor, praise, adoration,
Now and forever more be Thine.
slides.label: Verse 5

slides.text:
Faith of our fathers! living still,
In spite of dungeon, fire and sword;
Oh how our hearts beat high with joy
Whene'er we hear that glorious Word!
slides.label: Verse 1

slides.text:
Faith of our fathers, holy faith!
We will be true to thee till death.
slides.label: Chorus

slides.text:
Our fathers, chained in prisons dark,
Were still in heart and conscience free:
How sweet would be their children's fate,
If they, like them, could die for Thee!
slides.label: Verse 2

slides.text:
Faith of our fathers, holy faith!
We will be true to thee till death.
slides.label: Chorus

slides.text:
Faith of our fathers! we will strive
To win all nations unto Thee;
And through the truth that comes from God,
We all shall then be truly free.
slides.label: Verse 3

slides.text:
Faith of our fathers, holy faith!
We will be true to thee till death.
slides.label: Chorus

slides.text:
Faith of our fathers! we will love
Both friend and foe in all our strife;
And preach Thee, too, as love knows how,
By kindly words and virtuous life.
slides.label: Verse 4

slides.text:
Faith of our fathers, holy faith!
We will be true to thee till death.
slides.label: Chorus

slides.text:
Fight the good fight with all thy might,
Christ is thy strength, and Christ thy right;
Lay hold on life, and it shall be
Thy joy and crown eternally.
slides.label: Verse 1

slides.text:
Run the straight race through God’s good grace,
Lift up thine eyes and seek His face;
Life with its way before thee lies,
Christ is the path, and Christ the prize.
slides.label: Verse 2
Verse 3

slides.text:
Fill thou my life, O Lord my God,
In every part with praise,
That my whole being may proclaim
Thy being and Thy ways.
slides.label: Verse 1

slides.text:
Not for the lip of praise alone,
Nor e’en the praising heart
I ask, but for a life made up
Of praise in every part:
slides.label: Verse 2

slides.text:
Praise in the common things of life,
Its goings out and in;
Praise in each duty and each deed,
However small and mean.
slides.label: Verse 3

slides.text:
Fill every part of me with praise;
Let all my being speak
Of Thee and of Thy love, O Lord,
Poor though I be and weak.
slides.label: Verse 4

slides.text:
So shall Thou, gracious Lord, from me
Receive the glory due;
And so shall I begin on earth
The song forever new.
slides.label: Verse 5

slides.text:
So shall no part of day or night
From sacredness be free;
But all my life, in every step,
Be fellowship with Thee.
slides.label: Verse 6

slides.text:
For all the saints, who from their labours rest,
Who Thee by faith before the world confessed,
Thy name, O Jesus, be forever blest.
Hallelujah! Hallelujah!
slides.label: Verse 1
Verse 2

slides.text:
O may Thy soldiers, faithful, true and bold,
Fight as the saints who nobly fought of old,
And win, with them, the victor’s crown of gold!
Hallelujah! Hallelujah!
O blest communion, fellowship divine!
We feebly struggle, they in glory shine;
Yet all are one in Thee, for all are Thine.
Hallelujah! Hallelujah!
slides.label: Verse 3

slides.text:
And when the strife is fierce, the warfare long,
Steals on the ear the distant triumph song,
And hearts are brave again, and arms are strong.
Hallelujah! Hallelujah!
slides.label: Verse 4
Verse 5
Verse 6

slides.text:
From earth’s wide bounds, from ocean’s farthest coast,
Through gates of pearl streams in the countless host,
Singing to Father, Son and Holy Ghost.
Hallelujah! Hallelujah!
slides.label: Verse 7

title: For the Beauty of the Earth
author: Folliot S. Pierpoint

slides.text:
For the beauty of the earth,
For the beauty of the skies,
For the love which from our birth
Over and around us lies:
Father, unto Thee we raise
This our sacrifice of praise.
slides.label: Verse 1

slides.text:
For the beauty of each hour
Of the day and of the night,
Hill and vale, and tree and flower,
Sun and moon, and stars of light:
Father, unto Thee we raise
This our sacrifice of praise.
slides.label: Verse 2

slides.text:
For the joy of human love,
Brother, sister, parent, child,
Friends on earth, and friends above;
For all gentle thoughts and mild:
Father, unto Thee we raise
This our sacrifice of praise.
slides.label: Verse 3

slides.text:
For each perfect gift of Thine
To our race so freely given,
Graces, human and divine,
Flowers of earth, and buds of heaven:
Father, unto Thee we raise
This our sacrifice of praise.
slides.label: Verse 4

title: Forth in Thy Name, O Lord, I Go
author: Charles Wesley

slides.text:
Forth in Thy name, O Lord, I go,
My daily labour to pursue,
Thee, only Thee, resolved to know
In all I think, or speak, or do.
slides.label: Verse 1

slides.text:
The task Thy wisdom hath assigned
O let me cheerfully fulfil;
In all my works Thy presence find,
And prove Thy acceptable will.
slides.label: Verse 2

slides.text:
Thee may I set at my right hand,
Whose eyes my inmost substance see;
And labour on at Thy command,
And offer all my works to Thee.
slides.label: Verse 3

slides.text:
Give me to bear Thy easy yoke,
And every moment watch and pray,
And still to things eternal look,
And hasten to Thy glorious day.
slides.label: Verse 4

slides.text:
For Thee delightfully employ
Whate'er Thy bounteous grace hath given,
And run my course with even joy,
And closely walk with Thee to heaven.
slides.label: Verse 5

title: From All That Dwell Below the Skies
author: Isaac Watts

slides.text:
From all that dwell below the skies
Let the Creator’s praise arise:
Alleluia! Alleluia!
Let the Redeemer’s name be sung
Through every land, by every tongue.
slides.label: Verse 1

slides.text:
Alleluia! Alleluia!
Alleluia! Alleluia!
Alleluia!
slides.label: Verse 2

slides.text:
Eternal are Thy mercies, Lord;
Eternal truth attends Thy word:
Alleluia! Alleluia!
Thy praise shall sound from shore to shore,
Till suns shall rise and set no more.
slides.label: Verse 3

slides.text:
Your lofty themes, ye mortals, bring,
In songs of praise divinely sing:
Alleluia! Alleluia!
The great salvation loud proclaim,
And shout for joy the Saviour’s name.
slides.label: Verse 4

slides.text:
In every land begin the song;
To every land the strains belong.
Alleluia! Alleluia!
In cheerful sounds all voices raise,
And fill the world with loudest praise.
slides.label: Verse 5

title: Glorious Things of Thee are Spoken
author: John Newton

slides.text:
Glorious things of Thee are spoken,
Zion, city of our God!
He whose word cannot be broken
Formed thee for His own abode.
On the Rock of Ages founded,
What can shake thy sure repose?
With salvation’s walls surrounded,
Thou mayest smile at all thy foes.
slides.label: Verse 1

slides.text:
See! The streams of living waters,
Springing from eternal love,
Well supply thy sons and daughters,
And all fear of want remove;
Who can faint, whilst such a river
Ever flows their thirst to assuage?
Grace which, like the Lord, the Giver,
Never fails from age to age.
slides.label: Verse 2

slides.text:
Round each habitation hovering,
See the cloud and fire appear!
For a glory and a covering,
Showing that the Lord is near.
He who gives them daily manna,
He who listens when they cry:
Let Him hear the loud hosanna
Rising to His throne on high.
slides.label: Verse 3

slides.text:
Saviour, if of Zion’s city
I, through grace, a member am,
Let the world deride or pity,
I will glory in Thy name.
Fading is the worldling’s pleasure,
All his boasted pomp and show,
Solid joys and lasting treasure
None but Zion’s children know.
slides.label: Verse 4

title: Glory To His Name
author: Elisha A. Hoffman, John H. Stockton

slides.text:
Down at the cross where my Savior died,
Down where for cleansing from sin I cried,
There to my heart was the blood applied;
Glory to His Name!
slides.label: Verse 1
Chorus 1
Verse 2

title: Go Tell It on the Mountain
author: African-American spiritual; John W. Work, Jr.

slides.text:
Go, tell it on the mountain,
Over the hills and everywhere
Go, tell it on the mountain,
That Jesus Christ is born.
slides.label: Chorus

slides.text:
While shepherds kept their watching
O'er silent flocks by night
Behold throughout the heavens
There shone a holy light.
slides.label: Verse 1

slides.text:
Go, tell it on the mountain,
Over the hills and everywhere
Go, tell it on the mountain,
That Jesus Christ is born.
slides.label: Chorus

slides.text:
The shepherds feared and trembled,
When lo! above the earth,
Rang out the angel chorus
That hailed the Savior's birth.
slides.label: Verse 2

slides.text:
Go, tell it on the mountain,
Over the hills and everywhere
Go, tell it on the mountain,
That Jesus Christ is born.
slides.label: Chorus

slides.text:
Down in a lowly manger
The humble Christ was born
And God sent us salvation
That blessèd Christmas morn.
slides.label: Verse 3

slides.text:
Go, tell it on the mountain,
Over the hills and everywhere
Go, tell it on the mountain,
That Jesus Christ is born.
slides.label: Chorus

title: God is Working His Purpose Out
author: Arthur C. Ainger

slides.text:
God is working His purpose out,
As year succeeds to year;
God is working His purpose out,
And the time is drawing near;
Nearer and nearer draws the time,
The time that shall surely be,
When the earth shall be filled
With the glory of God,
As the waters cover the sea.
slides.label: Verse 1

slides.text:
From utmost East to utmost West,
Where’er man’s foot hath trod,
By the mouth of many messengers
Goes forth the voice of God;
Give ear to Me, ye continents,
Ye isles, give ear to Me,
That the earth may be filled
With the glory of God,
As the waters cover the sea.
slides.label: Verse 2

slides.text:
March we forth in the strength of God
With the banner of Christ unfurled,
That the light of the glorious gospel of truth
May shine throughout the world:
Fight we the fight with sorrow and sin,
To set their captives free,
That the earth may be filled
With the glory of God,
As the waters cover the sea.
slides.label: Verse 3

slides.text:
All we can do is nothing worth,
Unless God blesses the deed;
Vainly we hope for the harvest-tide
Till God gives life to the seed;
Yet nearer and nearer draws the time,
The time that shall surely be,
When the earth shall be filled
With the glory of God,
As the waters cover the sea.
slides.label: Verse 4

title: God Of Our Fathers
author: Daniel C. Roberts, George W. Warren

slides.text:
God of our fathers, whose almighty hand
Leads forth in beauty all the starry band
Of shining worlds in splendor through the skies,
Our grateful songs before Thy throne arise.
slides.label: Verse 1

slides.text:
Thy love divine hath led us in the past,
In this free land by Thee our lot is cast;
Be Thou our ruler, guardian, guide, and stay,
Thy Word our law, Thy paths our chosen way.
slides.label: Verse 2

slides.text:
God rest ye merry, gentlemen,
Let nothing you dismay,
Remember Christ our Savior
Was born on Christmas Day;
To save us all from Satan's power
When we were gone astray.
slides.label: Verse 1
Chorus

slides.text:
In Bethlehem, in Israel,
This blessèd Babe was born,
And laid within a manger
Upon this blessèd morn;
The which His mother Mary
Did nothing take in scorn.
slides.label: Verse 2
Chorus
Verse 3
Chorus

slides.text:
Fear not, then, said the angel,
Let nothing you affright
This day is born a Savior
Of a pure virgin bright,
To free all those who trust in Him
From Satan's power and might.
slides.label: Verse 4
Chorus

slides.text:
The shepherds at those tidings
Rejoicèd much in mind,
And left their flocks a-feeding
In tempest, storm and wind,
And went to Bethl'em straightaway
This blessèd Babe to find.
slides.label: Verse 5
Chorus

slides.text:
But when to Bethlehem they came
Where our dear Savior lay,
They found Him in a manger
Where oxen feed on hay;
His mother Mary kneeling
Unto the Lord did pray.
slides.label: Verse 6
Chorus

slides.text:
Now to the Lord sing praises
All you within this place,
And with true love and brotherhood
Each other now embrace;
This holy tide of Christmas
All others doth deface.
slides.label: Verse 7
Chorus

slides.text:
God bless the ruler of this house,
And send him long to reign,
And many a merry Christmas
May live to see again;
Among your friends and kindred
That live both far and near—
slides.label: Verse 8

slides.text:
That God send you a happy new year,
Happy new year,
And God send you a happy new year.
slides.label: Verse 9
Verse 1

slides.text:
Good Christian men, rejoice
With heart and soul and voice;
Now ye hear of endless bliss,
Jesus Christ was born for this:
He hath opened heaven’s door
And man is blessed forever more.
Christ was born for this;
Christ was born for this!
slides.label: Verse 2
Verse 3

slides.text:
Good King Wenceslas looked out
On the Feast of Stephen,
When the snow lay round about,
Deep and crisp and even.
Brightly shone the moon that night,
Though the frost was cruel,
When a poor man came in sight,
Gathering winter fuel.
slides.label: Verse 1

slides.text:
Hither, page, and stand by me,
If you know it, telling,
Yonder peasant, who is he?
Where and what his dwelling?
Sire, he lives a good league hence,
Underneath the mountain,
Right against the forest fence,
By Saint Agnes' fountain.
slides.label: Verse 2

slides.text:
Bring me flesh, and bring me wine,
Bring me pine logs hither,
You and I will see him dine,
When we bear them thither.
Page and monarch, forth they went,
Forth they went together,
Through the cold wind's wild lament
And the bitter weather.
slides.label: Verse 3

slides.text:
Sire, the night is darker now,
And the wind blows stronger,
Fails my heart, I know not how;
I can go no longer.
Mark my footsteps, my good page,
Tread now in them boldly,
You shall find the winter's rage
Freeze your blood less coldly.
slides.label: Verse 4

slides.text:
In his master's steps he trod,
Where the snow lay dinted;
Heat was in the very sod
Which the saint had printed.
Therefore, Christian men, be sure,
Wealth or rank possessing,
You who now will bless the poor
Shall yourselves find blessing.
slides.label: Verse 5

title: Guide Me O Thou Great Jehovah
author: William Williams

slides.text:
Guide me, O thou great Jehovah,
Pilgrim through this barren land;
I am weak, but Thou art mighty,
Hold me with Thy powerful hand:
Bread of heaven, Bread of heaven,
Feed me now and ever more,
Feed me now and ever more.
slides.label: Verse 1

slides.text:
Open Thou the crystal fountain
Whence the healing stream doth flow;
Let the fiery, cloudy pillar
Lead me all my journey through:
Strong Deliverer, strong Deliverer,
Be Thou still my strength and shield,
Be Thou still my strength and shield.
slides.label: Verse 2

slides.text:
When I tread the verge of Jordan
Bid my anxious fears subside;
Death of death, and hell’s destruction,
Land me safe on Canaan’s side:
Songs of praises, songs of praises,
I will ever give to Thee,
I will ever give to Thee.
slides.label: Verse 3

slides.text:
Hail, thou once despised Jesus,
Hail, Thou Galilean King!
Thou didst suffer to release us,
Thou didst free salvation bring.
Hail, Thou agonising Saviour,
Bearer of our sin and shame;
By Thy merits we find favour,
Life is given through Thy name.
slides.label: Verse 1

slides.text:
Paschal Lamb, by God appointed,
All our sins on Thee were laid.
With almighty love anointed
Thou hast full atonement made.
All Thy people are forgiven
Through the virtue of Thy blood:
Opened is the gate of heaven,
Man is reconciled to God.
slides.label: Verse 2

slides.text:
Jesus, hail! enthroned in glory,
There forever to abide;
All the heavenly hosts adore Thee,
Seated at Thy Father’s side:
There for sinners Thou art pleading,
There Thou dost our place prepare,
Ever for us interceding,
Till in glory we appear.
slides.label: Verse 3

slides.text:
Worship, honour, power, and blessing
Thou art worthy to receive:
Loudest praises, without ceasing,
Right it is for us to give:
Come, O mighty Holy Spirit,
As our hearts and hands we raise,
Help us sing our Saviour’s merits,
Help us sing Immanuel’s praise.
slides.label: Verse 4

slides.text:
Hail to the Lord's anointed,
Great David’s greater Son!
Hail, in the time appointed,
His reign on earth begun!
He comes to break oppression,
To set the captive free,
To take away transgression,
And rule in equity.
slides.label: Verse 1

slides.text:
He comes, with succour speedy,
To those who suffer wrong;
To help the poor and needy,
And bid the weak be strong;
To give them songs for sighing,
Their darkness turn to light,
Whose souls, condemned and dying,
Were precious in His sight.
slides.label: Verse 2
Verse 3

slides.text:
Kings shall fall down before Him,
And gold and incense bring;
All nations shall adore Him,
His praise all people sing;
To Him shall prayer unceasing
And daily vows ascend,
His kingdom still increasing,
A kingdom without end.
slides.label: Verse 4

slides.text:
O’er every foe victorious,
He on His throne shall rest;
From age to age more glorious,
All-blessing and all-blessed.
The tide of time shall never
His covenant remove;
His name shall stand forever,
His changeless name of Love.
slides.label: Verse 5

slides.text:
Hallelujah! Sing to Jesus;
His the sceptre, His the throne;
Hallelujah! His the triumph,
His the victory alone.
Hark, the songs of holy Zion
Thunder like a mighty flood:
‘Jesus out of every nation
Hath redeemed us by His blood.’
slides.label: Verse 1

slides.text:
Hallelujah! not as orphans
Are we left in sorrow now;
Hallelujah! He is near us,
Faith believes, nor questions how.
Though the clouds from sight receivedHim
When the forty days were o’er,
Shall our hearts forget His promise,
‘I am with you ever more’?
slides.label: Verse 2

slides.text:
Hallelujah! Bread of heaven,
Thou on earth our food, our stay;
Hallelujah! here the sinful
Flee to Thee from day to day.
Intercessor, Friend of sinners,
Earth’s Redeemer, plead for me
Where the songs of all the sinless
Sweep across the crystal sea.
slides.label: Verse 3

slides.text:
Hallelujah! sing to Jesus;
His the sceptre, His the throne;
Hallelujah! His the triumph,
His the victory alone.
Hark, the songs of holy Zion
Thunder like a mighty flood:
‘Jesus out of every nation
Hath redeemed us by His blood.’
slides.label: Verse 4

slides.text:
Hark the glad sound! The Saviour comes,
The Saviour promised long;
Let every heart prepare a throne,
And every voice a song.
slides.label: Verse 1

slides.text:
He comes the prisoners to release,
In Satan’s bondage held;
The gates of brass before Him burst,
The iron fetters yield.
slides.label: Verse 2

slides.text:
He comes the broken heart to bind,
The bleeding soul to cure,
And with the treasures of His grace
To enrich the humble poor.
slides.label: Verse 3

slides.text:
Our glad hosannas, Prince of Peace,
Thy welcome shall proclaim;
And heaven’s eternal arches ring
With Thy beloved name.
slides.label: Verse 4

slides.text:
Hark! The herald angels sing:
‘Glory to the new-born King!
Peace on earth, and mercy mild,
God and sinners reconciled!’
slides.label: Verse 1

slides.text:
Joyful, all ye nations rise,
Join the triumph of the skies,
With the angelic host proclaim,
‘Christ is born in Bethlehem.’
slides.label: Verse 2

slides.text:
Hark! the herald angels sing:
‘Glory to the new-born King!’
Christ, by highest heaven adored,
Christ, the everlasting Lord,
slides.label: Verse 3

slides.text:
Late in time behold Him come,
Offspring of a virgin’s womb.
Veiled in flesh the Godhead see!
Hail the incarnate Deity!
slides.label: Verse 4

slides.text:
Pleased as man with man to dwell,
Jesus, our Immanuel.
Hark! the herald angels sing:
‘Glory to the new-born King.’
slides.label: Verse 5

slides.text:
Hail the heaven-born Prince of Peace!
Hail, the Sun of righteousness!
Light and life to all He brings,
Risen with healing in His wings,
slides.label: Verse 6
Verse 7

slides.text:
He who would valiant be
’Gainst all disaster,
Let him in constancy
Follow the Master.
There’s no discouragement
Shall make him once relent
His first avowed intent
To be a pilgrim.
slides.label: Verse 1

slides.text:
Who so beset him round
With dismal stories,
Do but themselves confound—
His strength the more is.
No foes shall stay his might,
Though he with giants fight;
He will make good his right
To be a pilgrim.
slides.label: Verse 2

slides.text:
Since, Lord, Thou dost defend
Us with Thy Spirit,
We know we at the end
Shall life inherit.
Then fancies flee away!
I’ll fear not what men say,
I’ll labour night and day
To be a pilgrim.
slides.label: Verse 3

slides.text:
Here is love vast as the ocean,
Loving kindness as the flood,
When the Prince of life, our ransom
Shed for us His precious blood.
Who His love will not remember?
Who can cease to sing His praise?
He can never be forgotten
Throughout heaven’s eternal days.
slides.label: Verse 1

slides.text:
On the Mount of Crucifixion
Fountains opened deep and wide;
Through the floodgates of God’s mercy
Flowed a vast and gracious tide.
Grace and love, like mighty rivers,
Poured incessant from above,
And heaven’s peace and perfect justice
Kissed a guilty world in love.
slides.label: Verse 2

slides.text:
I'm pressing on the upward way,
New heights I'm gaining every day;
Still praying as I'm onward bound,
Lord, plant my feet on higher ground.
slides.label: Verse 1

slides.text:
Lord, lift me up and let me stand,
By faith, on Heaven's table land,
A higher plane than I have found;
Lord, plant my feet on higher ground.
slides.label: Chorus

slides.text:
My heart has no desire to stay
Where doubts arise and fears dismay;
Though some may dwell where those abound,
My prayer, my aim, is higher ground.
slides.label: Verse 2

slides.text:
Lord, lift me up and let me stand,
By faith, on Heaven's table land,
A higher plane than I have found;
Lord, plant my feet on higher ground.
slides.label: Chorus

slides.text:
I want to live above the world,
Though Satan's darts at me are hurled;
For faith has caught the joyful sound,
The song of saints on higher ground.
slides.label: Verse 3

slides.text:
Lord, lift me up and let me stand,
By faith, on Heaven's table land,
A higher plane than I have found;
Lord, plant my feet on higher ground.
slides.label: Chorus

slides.text:
I want to scale the utmost height
And catch a gleam of glory bright;
But still I'll pray till Heav'n I've found,
Lord, plant my feet on higher ground.
slides.label: Verse 4

slides.text:
Lord, lift me up and let me stand,
By faith, on Heaven's table land,
A higher plane than I have found;
Lord, plant my feet on higher ground.
slides.label: Chorus

title: Holy Holy Holy Lord God Almighty
author: Reginald Heber

slides.text:
Holy, holy, holy, Lord God almighty!
Early in the morning
Our song shall rise to Thee:
Holy, holy, holy, merciful and mighty,
God in three Persons, blessed Trinity!
slides.label: Verse 1

slides.text:
Holy, holy, holy! all the saints adore Thee,
Casting down their golden crowns
Around the glassy sea;
Cherubim and seraphim falling down before Thee,
Who were, and are, and ever more shall be.
slides.label: Verse 2

slides.text:
Holy, holy, holy! though the darkness hide Thee,
Though the eye of sinful man
Thy glory may not see;
Only Thou art holy, there is none beside Thee,
Perfect in power, in love and purity.
slides.label: Verse 3

slides.text:
Holy, holy, holy, Lord God Almighty!
All Thy works shall praise Thy name
In earth, and sky, and sea;
Holy, holy, holy, merciful and mighty,
God in three Persons, blessed Trinity!
slides.label: Verse 4

slides.text:
Hosanna, loud hosanna,
The little children sang;
Through pillared court and temple
The lovely anthem rang.
To Jesus, who had blessed them
Close folded to His breast,
The children sang their praises,
The simplest and the best.
slides.label: Verse 1

slides.text:
From Olivet they followed
Mid an exultant crowd,
The victor palm branch waving,
And chanting clear and loud;
Bright angels joined the chorus,
Beyond the cloudless sky,
Hosanna in the highest,
Glory to God on high!
slides.label: Verse 2

slides.text:
Fair leaves of silvery olive
They strewed upon the ground,
While Salem's circling mountains
Echoed the joyful sound;
The Lord of men and angels
Rode on in lowly state,
Nor scorned that little children
Should on His bidding wait.
slides.label: Verse 3

slides.text:
Hosanna in the highest!
That ancient song we sing,
For Christ is our Redeemer,
The Lord of Heaven our king.
O may we ever praise Him
With heart and life and voice,
And in His blissful presence
Eternally rejoice!
slides.label: Verse 4

slides.text:
Hover o'er me, Holy Spirit,
Bathe my trembling heart and brow;
Fill me with Thy hallowed presence,
Come, O come and fill me now.
slides.label: Verse 1

slides.text:
Fill me now, fill me now,
Jesus, come and fill me now.
Fill me with Thy hallowed presence,
Jesus, come and fill me now.
slides.label: Verse 2

slides.text:
Thou can fill me, gracious Spirit,
Though I cannot tell Thee how;
But I need Thee, greatly need Thee,
Come, O come and fill me now.
slides.label: Verse 3

slides.text:
I am weakness, full of weakness,
At Thy sacred feet I bow;
Blest, divine, eternal Spirit,
Come with power, and fill me now.
slides.label: Verse 4

slides.text:
How firm a foundation, ye saints of the Lord,
Is laid for your faith in His excellent Word!
What more can He say than to you He hath said,
You, who unto Jesus for refuge have fled?
slides.label: Verse 1
Verse 2

slides.text:
Fear not, I am with thee, O be not dismayed,
For I am thy God and will still give thee aid;
I'll strengthen and help thee, and cause thee to stand
Upheld by My righteous, omnipotent hand.
slides.label: Verse 3

slides.text:
When through the deep waters I call thee to go,
The rivers of woe shall not thee overflow;
For I will be with thee, thy troubles to bless,
And sanctify to thee thy deepest distress.
slides.label: Verse 4

slides.text:
When through fiery trials thy pathways shall lie,
My grace, all sufficient, shall be thy supply;
The flame shall not hurt thee; I only design
Thy dross to consume, and thy gold to refine.
slides.label: Verse 5

slides.text:
Even down to old age all My people shall prove
My sovereign, eternal, unchangeable love;
And when hoary hairs shall their temples adorn,
Like lambs they shall still in My bosom be borne.
slides.label: Verse 6

slides.text:
The soul that on Jesus has leaned for repose,
I will not, I will not desert to its foes;
That soul, though all hell should endeavor to shake,
I'll never, no never, no never forsake.
slides.label: Verse 7

title: How Sweet the name of Jesus Sounds
author: John Newton

slides.text:
How sweet the name of Jesus sounds
In a believer’s ear!
It soothes his sorrows, heals his wounds,
And drives away his fear.
slides.label: Verse 1

slides.text:
It makes the wounded spirit whole,
And calms the troubled breast;
’Tis manna to the hungry soul,
And to the weary, rest.
slides.label: Verse 2

slides.text:
Dear name, the rock on which I build,
My shield and hiding place,
My never-failing treasury, filled
With boundless stores of grace!
slides.label: Verse 3

slides.text:
Jesus! My Shepherd, Saviour, Friend,
My Prophet, Priest and King,
My Lord, my Life, my Way, my End,
Accept the praise I bring.
slides.label: Verse 4

slides.text:
Weak is the effort of my heart,
And cold my warmest thought;
But when I see Thee as Thou art,
I’ll praise Thee as I ought.
slides.label: Verse 5

slides.text:
Till then I would Thy love proclaim
With every fleeting breath;
And may the music of Thy name
Refresh my soul in death.
slides.label: Verse 6

slides.text:
I am Thine, O Lord, I have heard Thy voice,
And it told Thy love to me;
But I long to rise in the arms of faith
And be closer drawn to Thee.
slides.label: Verse 1

slides.text:
Draw me nearer, nearer blessèd Lord,
To the cross where Thou hast died.
Draw me nearer, nearer, nearer blessèd Lord,
To Thy precious, bleeding side.
slides.label: Chorus

slides.text:
Consecrate me now to Thy service, Lord,
By the power of grace divine;
Let my soul look up with a steadfast hope,
And my will be lost in Thine.
slides.label: Verse 2

slides.text:
Draw me nearer, nearer blessèd Lord,
To the cross where Thou hast died.
Draw me nearer, nearer, nearer blessèd Lord,
To Thy precious, bleeding side.
slides.label: Chorus

slides.text:
O the pure delight of a single hour
That before Thy throne I spend,
When I kneel in prayer, and with Thee, my God
I commune as friend with friend!
slides.label: Verse 3

slides.text:
Draw me nearer, nearer blessèd Lord,
To the cross where Thou hast died.
Draw me nearer, nearer, nearer blessèd Lord,
To Thy precious, bleeding side.
slides.label: Chorus

slides.text:
There are depths of love that I cannot know
Till I cross the narrow sea;
There are heights of joy that I may not reach
Till I rest in peace with Thee.
slides.label: Verse 4

slides.text:
Draw me nearer, nearer blessèd Lord,
To the cross where Thou hast died.
Draw me nearer, nearer, nearer blessèd Lord,
To Thy precious, bleeding side.
slides.label: Chorus

title: I am Trusting Thee Lord Jesus
author: Frances Ridley Havergal

slides.text:
I am trusting Thee, Lord Jesus,
Trusting only Thee!
Trusting Thee for full salvation,
Great and free.
slides.label: Verse 1

slides.text:
I am trusting Thee for pardon,
At Thy feet I bow;
For Thy grace and tender mercy,
Trusting now.
slides.label: Verse 2

slides.text:
I am trusting Thee for cleansing
In the crimson flood;
Trusting Thee to make me holy,
By Thy blood.
slides.label: Verse 3

slides.text:
I am trusting Thee for power,
Thine can never fail;
Words which Thou Thyself shalt give me
Must prevail.
slides.label: Verse 4

slides.text:
I am trusting Thee to guide me,
Thou alone shalt lead;
Every day and hour supplying
All my need.
slides.label: Verse 5
Verse 6

slides.text:
I cannot tell why He, whom angels worship,
Should set His love upon the sons of men,
Or why, as Shepherd, He should seek the wanderers,
To bring them back, they know not how or when.
But this I know, that He was born of Mary,
When Bethlehem’s manger was His only home,
And that He lived at Nazareth and laboured,
And so the Saviour, Saviour of the world, is come.
slides.label: Verse 1

slides.text:
I cannot tell how silently He suffered,
As with His peace He graced this place of tears,
Or how His heart upon the cross wasbroken,
The crown of pain to three-and-thirty years.
But this I know, He heals the broken-hearted,
And stays our sin, and calms our lurkingfear,
And lifts the burden from the heavy-laden,
For yet the Saviour, Saviour of the world, is here.
slides.label: Verse 2

slides.text:
I cannot tell how He will win the nations,
How He will claim His earthly heritage,
How satisfy the needs and aspirations
Of east and west, of sinner and of sage.
But this I know, all flesh shall see His glory,
And He shall reap the harvest He has sown,
And some glad day His sun shall shine in splendour,
When He the Saviour, Saviour of the world, is known.
slides.label: Verse 3

slides.text:
I cannot tell how all the lands shall worship,
When, at his bidding, every storm is stilled,
Or who can say how great the jubilation
When all the hearts of men with love are filled.
But this I know, the skies will thrill with rapture,
And myriad, myriad human voices sing,
And earth to heaven, and heaven to earth, will answer:
‘At last the Saviour, Saviour of the world, is King!’
slides.label: Verse 4

title: I Heard the Voice of Jesus Say
author: Horatius Bonar

slides.text:
I heard the voice of Jesus say:
‘Come unto Me and rest;
Lay down, thou weary one, lay down
Thy head upon My breast.’
I came to Jesus as I was,
Weary and worn and sad;
I found in Him a resting place,
And He has made me glad.
slides.label: Verse 1

slides.text:
I heard the voice of Jesus say:
‘Behold I freely give
The living water, thirsty one,
Stoop down and drink and live.’
I came to Jesus, and I drank
Of that life-giving stream;
My thirst was quenched, my soul revived,
slides.label: Verse 2

slides.text:
And now I live in Him.
I heard the voice of Jesus say:
‘I am this dark world’s light;
Look unto Me, thy morn shall rise,
And all thy day be bright.’
I looked to Jesus, and I found
In Him my Star, my Sun;
And in that light of life I’ll walk,
Till travelling days are done.
slides.label: Verse 3

title: I Know Not Why God's Wondrous Grace
author: D. W. Whittle

slides.text:
I know not why God's wondrous grace
To me hath been made known;
Nor why, unworthy as I am,
He claimed me for His own.
slides.label: Verse 1

slides.text:
But I know whom I have believed;
And am persuaded that He is able
To keep that which I’ve committed
Unto Him against that day.
slides.label: Verse 2

slides.text:
I know not how this saving faith
To me He did impart;
Or how believing in His word
Wrought peace within my heart.
slides.label: Verse 3

slides.text:
I know not how the Spirit moves,
Convincing men of sin;
Revealing Jesus through the word,
Creating faith in Him.
slides.label: Verse 4

slides.text:
I know not what of good or ill
May be reserved for me,
Of weary ways or golden days
Before His face I see.
slides.label: Verse 5
Verse 6
